intro: We describe our home when we introduce ourselves, look for a flat, invite someone or explain where something is. This lesson gives you rooms, furniture and sentences to describe a home, with the traps of floors and “at home”.
objectifs: Name types of home, rooms and common furniture.
Describe your home with there is / there are, have got and adjectives.
Use floors correctly (ground floor, first floor) and upstairs / downstairs.

texte: A home in a building is “a flat” in British English and “an apartment” in American and Canadian English. “A house” is a building for one family; “a studio” (UK also “studio flat”) is a flat with one main room.

Floors: in British English, the floor at street level is “the ground floor” and the floor above it is “the first floor”. In American English, the floor at street level is “the first floor”! Use the preposition “on”: “on the second floor”.
“Upstairs” = on a higher floor; “downstairs” = on a lower floor. Use them with no preposition: “The bedrooms are upstairs.”

lignes: a machine to go up and down

exemples: I live in a flat on the fourth floor.

texte: Many room names are compound words: bed + room = bedroom, bath + room = bathroom. Say “in the kitchen”, “in the living room”.

“Toilet” is the room with a toilet at home (UK informal: “the loo”). In a public place, say “the toilets” or “the ladies / the gents” (UK) and “the restroom” (US). “Bathroom” is the room with a bath or shower; Americans also use it for the toilet.

lignes: come in, take off your coat

exemples: The children are in the garden.
Our flat has got two bedrooms and a small kitchen.
have got to describe a home.
sections.note: Careful: “a cave” is a big hole in a mountain or under the ground. The room under a house for wine or old things is “the cellar” (or “the basement”). For the room where you sleep, say “bedroom”, not “chamber”.

texte: “Furniture” is uncountable: “There's a lot of furniture.” For one thing, say “a piece of furniture”.
“A cupboard” has doors and shelves, often in the kitchen; “a wardrobe” is a tall cupboard for clothes (US: “closet”).

lignes: a sofa · an armchair · a coffee table · a TV · a lamp · a carpet
sofa: for two or more people
a fridge · a cooker · a sink · a cupboard · a table
a bed · a wardrobe · a desk · a mirror · a chair
a shower · a bath · a washbasin · a towel

exemples: There's a big sofa in the living room.
The plates are in the cupboard next to the fridge.

texte: To describe a home, use tools you know: “there is / there are” (lesson 16), prepositions of place (lesson 17) and “have got” (lesson 5).
Useful adjectives: big / small, bright (with a lot of light), dark, quiet, noisy, modern, old, comfortable, clean, tidy (everything in its place), messy.
For renting: “rent” (the money you pay every month; to pay to live somewhere), “a landlord / a landlady” (the owner), “a neighbour” (US neighbor).
exemples: There are three bedrooms upstairs and there's a kitchen downstairs.
My flat is small but very bright.
The rent is 750 euros a month.

texte: “At home” = in your house or flat: “I'm at home.” Don't say “at the house” for your own home.
With a verb of movement, use “home” with no preposition: “go home”, “come home”, “get home” (arrive at home). Never “go to home”.
For someone else's home: “at Paul's” / “to Paul's”, or “at Paul's house / flat”.
exemples: I go home at six o'clock.
The party is at Julie's flat.

formule: There is / There are + room / furniture + place · on the first floor · upstairs / downstairs · at home, go home
prononciation: “comfortable” has three syllables: /ˈkʌmftəbl/ (“kumf-te-bl”), with the stress at the start.
“furniture” /ˈfɜːnɪtʃə/: stress on the first syllable, “ch” at the end.
In compound words, stress the first word: BEDroom, BATHroom, LIVing room.
“kitchen” /ˈkɪtʃɪn/: two short i sounds, with “ch” in the middle.
erreurs: No preposition between a verb of movement and “home”.
My flat is at the first floor.
My flat is on the first floor.
The room for sleeping = a bedroom.
We keep the wine in the cave.
We keep the wine in the cellar.
A cave is a hole in a mountain.

dialogue.contexte: In Brussels, Yasmine visits a flat to rent with the landlord, Mr Peeters.
lignes: Welcome! The flat is on the third floor. There's a lift.
Great. How many bedrooms are there?
There are two bedrooms, and a bathroom with a shower.
Oh, the living room is very bright! Is the furniture included?
Yes: the sofa, the table, the beds and the wardrobes.
And the kitchen? Is there a fridge?
Yes, there's a fridge and a new cooker. And there's a small balcony.

mots: I live in a small flat.
a home on one floor of a building (US: apartment)
The kitchen is next to the living room.
We watch TV in the living room.
the room where you relax and meet people
We live on the second floor.
a level of a building; the ground you walk on in a room
tables, chairs, beds and so on (uncountable)
There are flowers in the garden.
land next to a house with grass or flowers
The rent is high in Paris.
money you pay every month to live in a place

exercices.consigne: In which room do you do these things?
items: You watch TV with your family here.

exercices.consigne: In which room do you usually find this?
Complete with There's or There are.
items: ___ a lot of furniture in the living room.
___ a small garden behind the house.

exercices.consigne: Each sentence has one mistake. Write it correctly.
items: My flat is in the ground floor.
My flat is on the ground floor. (US: My apartment is on the first floor.)
There are a lot of furnitures.
I go to home at 6 p.m.

exercices.consigne: Describe your home in four or five sentences: the type of home, the floor, the rooms, your favourite room and what is in it.
items: I live in a flat in Yaoundé. It's on the second floor. There are two bedrooms, a living room, a kitchen and a bathroom. My favourite room is the living room: it's bright and there's a big comfortable sofa. There's also a small balcony with plants.

a_retenir: flat (UK) / apartment (US); ground floor (UK) = street level; first floor (UK) = the floor above; on the first floor.
Rooms: living room, kitchen, bedroom, bathroom, dining room, hall, garden.
“Furniture” is uncountable: a lot of furniture, a piece of furniture.
at home (in your home); go home, come home (no “to”).
To describe: There's a…, There are…, upstairs / downstairs, bright, quiet, comfortable.
